title: H-projectivity after factoring through a separated base morphism
statement: Let $f:Z\to T$ and $g:T\to B$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Suppose $g$ is separated, meaning that its diagonal $T\to T\times_B T$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Suppose $g\circ f$ is projective in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective]: for some integer $n\geq0$ there is a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_B$ over $B$. Then $f$ is projective in the same convention: there is a closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_T$ over $T$, with the same $n$.

source.place: Tag 0C4Q, lemma-projective-permanence, statement and proof; its closed-graph proof applied to a finite projective-space embedding yields the H-projective version with the same n. Projective-space base change: Tag 01WF, lemma-H-projective-base-change.

proof.text: Choose the given $B$-closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_B$ and write $q:\mathbf P^n_B\to B$ for its projection, so $q\circ i=g\circ f$, using [def-kun-projective]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-change-of-base-closed-immersion] to $f:Z\to T$, $\mathrm{id}_T:T\to T$ and the separated map $g:T\to B$. It gives a closed immersion $Z\times_TT\to Z\times_BT$. By the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], the first projection $Z\times_TT\to Z$ has inverse $(\mathrm{id}_Z,f)$: their composites have the identity projections. Under this isomorphism the displayed closed immersion is the graph $\gamma=(\mathrm{id}_Z,f):Z\to Z\times_BT$. Thus $\gamma$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 0C4Q, lemma-projective-permanence, first arrow in the factorization; schemes.tex Tags 01KS (lemma-semi-diagonal) and 01KR (lemma-fibre-product-after-map).

proof.text: Put $P=\mathbf P^n_B\times_BT$, and let $a:P\to\mathbf P^n_B$ be the first projection. The morphism $k:Z\times_BT\to P$ has components $(i\circ\mathrm{pr}_Z,\mathrm{pr}_T)$. It is a base change of $i$ along $a$: explicitly, $Z\times_{\mathbf P^n_B}P\cong Z\times_BT$ by the inverse maps $(z,(p,t))\mapsto(z,t)$ and $(z,t)\mapsto(z,(i(z),t))$. These formulas mean morphisms specified by their projections, and are inverse by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] to conclude that $k$ is a closed immersion. This uses no flatness hypothesis on $g$.

source.place: Tag 0C4Q, lemma-projective-permanence, second arrow as base change of a closed immersion; Tag 01QR, lemma-base-change-closed-immersion.

proof.text: Both $\gamma$ and $k$ are closed immersions, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp] makes $j=k\circ\gamma:Z\hookrightarrow P$ a closed immersion. Its two components are $i$ and $f$: the first is $i\circ\mathrm{pr}_Z\circ\gamma=i$ and the second is $\mathrm{pr}_T\circ\gamma=f$. Thus $j$ lies over $T$ with structural morphism $f$.

source.place: Tag 0C4Q, lemma-projective-permanence, composite factorization; Tag 01QS, lemma-composition-closed-immersion.

proof.text: Use [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback] for $g:T\to B$ and the finite homogeneous coordinate set $I=\{0,\ldots,n\}$. It identifies $\mathbf P(I;T)$ over $T$ with $T\times_B\mathbf P(I;B)$; interchange the two projections using [def-pc-fibre-product] to identify this with $P$. By [def-kun-projective], these are precisely $\mathbf P^n_T$ and $\mathbf P^n_B$. Composing $j$ with this isomorphism gives a closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_T$ whose projection is $f$. A closed immersion remains one under a target isomorphism directly from its definition [def-weil-closed-immersion]: the underlying closed embedding and the surjective structure-sheaf map are unchanged up to isomorphism. This is the factorization required by [def-kun-projective], with the original $n$.
